note: Curated Human-approved probes and separately identified LEARNED, VALIDATING historical discovery candidates. A probe is ACTIVE only from a HUMAN, APPROVED, counterexample-checked, generalized delta (see references/miss-probe-library.md). LEARNED records remain advisory SHADOW, never acceptance authority. Opaque case references resolve through the external mining ledger and never participate in matching. Never add a probe that encodes a single concrete symbol, path, or Jira key.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: value provenance beyond the authoring UI - repository node (CRX/DE), source map/topic file, API/import, and migration - and assert the product uses the correct source value

probes.abstraction_note: Any ticket where a value is written to an output must enumerate every channel the value can be set from, not only the authoring UI. The property NAME source and the property VALUE source can differ; the value is frequently read from the repository node. This generalizes beyond the originating metadata ticket to all value-write tickets.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: native platform features that share the touched asset upload, overwrite, or conflict flow - duplicate detection, versioning and timeline, DAM update-asset workflows, and processing profiles or metadata - enumerated as shared-path regression or their own acceptance criteria, not only the reported symptom

probes.abstraction_note: When a change touches a shared platform flow (asset upload/overwrite/conflict), the OTHER native product features that ride the same flow are shared-path consumers and must be enumerated, not just the reported symptom. Generalizes the CRX/DE value-provenance miss and the duplicate-detection miss into one shared-consumer rule.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: when the ticket names a specific UI mechanism to trigger an action (drag-and-drop, a button, right-click or context menu, a keyboard shortcut, or an API), enumerate the OTHER entry points for that same action and assert consistent behaviour across them

probes.abstraction_note: A mechanism named in Steps to Reproduce (e.g. drag-and-drop upload) is only one of several entry points for the action; the UAC must enumerate the sibling entry points, not only the one the reporter used. This is a stated-evidence enumeration miss, distinct from adjacent-feature discovery.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: when a ticket concerns an output-generation feature (Native PDF or any output), enumerate ALL generation entry points for that output - map/output-preset publishing, Map Collection publishing, single-topic generation, editor Download-as action, generate-for-review, and baseline/versioned publishing - and assert consistent behaviour across every entry point, not only the default preset-publish path; this applies to every output type (Native PDF, AEM Sites, HTML5, custom DITA-OT), not only PDF

probes.abstraction_note: Distinct from MP-003: MP-003 fires when the ticket NAMES a UI mechanism; MP-004 fires when the ticket names an OUTPUT-GENERATION feature that names NO entry point (e.g. 'Native PDF'). Such a feature always has several generation entry points sharing one engine, so the default preset-publish reading silently drops single-topic PDF, Download as PDF, review PDF, and baseline publishing.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: when a feature auto-derives or auto-populates an attribute or value onto a construct (for example a navigation/label/type attribute added on reference insertion), enumerate the full derivation surface, not only the one path the reporter used: (1) every insertion or trigger entry point (dialog, drag-and-drop, source typing, API) plus any explicit refresh or recompute action; (2) the construct's specializations, applying the derivation only where it is semantically valid and skipping resource-only or non-navigation variants; (3) reuse consumers of the derived value (keyref or conref, reuse across multiple parents, and cross-reference or link-text resolution); (4) editor parity across every editor that implements the population; (5) overwrite versus preserve of an existing author-set value; (6) the storage form (attribute versus element) and which form consumers read; (7) the fallback when the derivation source is empty, missing, external, or non-native

probes.abstraction_note: Generic enumeration for attribute-value derivation / auto-population features. Such a feature is never a single code path: the derived value flows through several insertion entry points, several specializations of the target construct, reuse consumers that read it, more than one editor, an explicit refresh action, and an overwrite policy, and it may live as an attribute or an element. Collapsing it to the one reporter-used path silently drops the rest. Complements MP-003 (stated UI mechanism) and MP-004 (output-generation entry points).

implied_dimension.candidate_template: locale granularity branch - a five-character regional locale (language plus region) versus the generic two-character language - assert the output uses the regional value when a regional entry exists and falls back to the generic value only when it does not

probes.abstraction_note: Any feature that resolves a localized value (labels, cross-reference strings, generated text) must be tested at both locale granularities: a regional locale must use its regional value when defined, not silently fall back to the generic language. Generalizes across all localized-value features and output engines.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: output-engine parity - for a rendering or output change, generate the same construct with Native PDF and with Direct DITA-OT and compare them; assert they agree on numbering, placement, ordering, and label text. A divergence is a defect unless an explicit product requirement documents it.

probes.abstraction_note: Cross-engine output-parity nuances (e.g. Native PDF using a TOC-local callout numbering sequence while DITA-OT preserves the shared number) produce no signal in ticket text, code grep, or spec - they only appear when both outputs are generated and diffed. This probe surfaces the parity dimension so it is not missed pre-UAC when no reviewer comment exists. VALIDATING until a second independent divergence case promotes it.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: investigate localized character input and rendering, plus localized resource paths and attachment interaction, on the touched flow; establish expected behaviour from current evidence

probes.abstraction_note: Historical theme-only incidents identify distinct localized input, snippet text, resource-path selection, and attachment interaction risks. They do not establish a shared root cause or accepted product behaviour; current applicability and expectations require investigation.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: investigate table header changes and multiple-row or column insertion and deletion on the touched editing flow; confirm applicable structural states and expected outcomes from current evidence

probes.abstraction_note: Separate historical reports cover header-row changes, multiple-column deletion, and multiple-row or column insertion. A generic text-alignment report is not counted as structural-table evidence. These reports suggest investigation, not automatic acceptance scope.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: investigate map-reference display and insertion behaviour; distinguish displayed reference text, inserted order, and error indicators using the current contract

probes.abstraction_note: Distinct reports support reference display, inserted topic order, and insertion error indicators. A duplicate display report is not counted independently. This is a reference-handling cluster, not evidence of multiple independently confirmed title-display misses or a universal title-versus-filename rule.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: asset-upload conflict dimensions: investigate and disposition content-identity duplicate detection and name/path conflicts separately before deciding acceptance coverage; establish the actual request handler and upload route independently from configuration artifacts; map the exact affected path, baseline actions, product-surface ownership, every named deployment, and documentation surface from applicable evidence without assuming parity

probes.abstraction_note: Asset-upload evidence can conflate content-identity duplicate detection, a same-name or path conflict, configuration metadata, request dispatch, deployment behavior, product-surface ownership, affected path, and baseline actions. These are independent dimensions. A matched probe requires investigation and disposition, not acceptance coverage for every dimension. A source scoped to one deployment or surface cannot establish another, matching labels or class names do not prove request routing, and native Assets actions such as Create Version and Overwrite Files are not Guides actions without source-backed ownership.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: when inspected implementation evidence places a shared backend collaborator in scope, enumerate every user-facing operation that reaches that same code and disposition each one as acceptance coverage, an explicit scope bound, or an open question; the operation named by the report is one caller among several, and a sibling entry point that shares the changed code is acceptance scope rather than background regression

probes.abstraction_note: A report names the operation the reporter performed, not the code that failed. When the failing collaborator is shared, the other operations that reach it inherit the same behaviour and the same risk, so authoring only from the reported operation silently drops them. Enumerating callers is a discovery obligation, not proof that every caller is affected: each enumerated entry point still requires its own disposition, and an operation the evidence shows cannot reach the code is bounded out explicitly rather than ignored.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: when a change makes an existing code path conditional, enumerate every observable outcome that path also produced and assert each remaining outcome explicitly; a path is rarely single purpose, so the outcomes incidental to the reported defect are the ones the change itself can silently remove

probes.abstraction_note: A fix that stops running a path in some case is read as removing one unwanted effect, but the same path commonly performs several effects, and only the unwanted one is under discussion. The remaining effects become fix-introduced regressions with no guard. This probe requires enumerating the skipped path's other outcomes and asserting them; it does not assert that any particular outcome is lost, which requires its own evidence.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: when implicated code resolves or queries data through the caller's own session or resolver, its results are filtered by that user's permissions; disposition what a user who cannot read a matched item observes, and require that the operation is not silently reported as though nothing matched

probes.abstraction_note: A lookup performed on the caller's behalf returns only what that caller may read, so the same operation can observe different state for different users without any code branch that mentions permissions. Testing as an administrator hides the entire dimension. The probe requires dispositioning the restricted-user outcome and the silent-no-match risk; it does not assert that hiding the item is wrong, which is a product decision.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: when a ticket is about two user operations colliding, enumerate every way EACH operation can start - UI actions, scheduled or delayed runs, approval workflows, bulk actions and APIs - and cover both sides, not only the operation the request names

probes.abstraction_note: A request to block operation A while operation B runs is usually written from the side of A, so the plan lists every way to start A and only the one way B happened in the incident. B's other start paths (scheduled, delayed, approved later, bulk, API) reach the same conflict and are silently untested. Cover the entry points of both operations; paths that start later than the click need their own check.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: for two colliding operations, disposition both orders - B starting while A runs and A starting while B runs - and check which order the reported incident actually followed; a safeguard for one order does not protect the other

probes.abstraction_note: A requested safeguard usually blocks one order of two operations. The incident evidence (timeline, logs) can show the other order, which the safeguard does not stop. Read the evidence timeline, name the incident order, and make the uncovered order an explicit AC or Open Question instead of assuming the request covers it.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: when an operation ends with a destructive step (delete orphans, purge, delete and recreate), check what happens if the main step fails partway: the destructive step must not run on partial results, and existing content must survive

probes.abstraction_note: Cleanup steps decide what to delete from what the current run produced. If an earlier error is only logged and the run continues, the cleanup sees an incomplete result and deletes content that should have stayed. Add a partial-failure check whenever the evidence shows a destructive step after the main work.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: when the ticket is about what a user can reach after a task or item changes state (completed, closed, done), state what that user can still do in the new state: open and read, reply to existing items, add new items, or nothing - and what stays blocked

probes.abstraction_note: Access tickets name the screen the user lost but rarely say which actions should come back. Restoring access can restore too much (editing a closed task) or too little (read only when replies are expected). Counterexample checked: a pure display defect with no state change does not need it.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: when the ticket asks for a missing validation error, check the reported invalid shape, the related invalid shapes of the same rule (one more, a span or reference past the limit), and the valid shapes next to the limit that must not raise a false error (fewer items, merged or spanned items, a corrected item)

probes.abstraction_note: A new validation is judged only on the reported example, so it is often too narrow (misses the other invalid shapes of the same rule) or too eager (flags valid content near the limit). Counterexample checked: a ticket that removes an existing error message needs only the regression side.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: when an embedded object (image, media, graphic) is resolved or rendered wrongly, check the same object in its other placements and forms: inside a table, a figure or a list, referenced by key, an SVG, and with width and height set

probes.abstraction_note: The reporter shows one image in one topic, but the resolving code serves every placement of the object. A fix that only handles the reported placement leaves the others broken. Counterexample checked: when the ticket names one placement as the only scope, the rest are out of scope.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: when the ticket makes a value available to output templates or changes which value is shown, list every place that value appears in the output (cover page, header, footer, table of contents, the file's document properties, output history) and check each one

probes.abstraction_note: A title or metadata value is read by several output places, not only the one in the screenshot. Changing or exposing it in one place leaves the others showing the old value. Counterexample checked: a value used by exactly one documented place needs no list.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: when a failure, a rejected request or an unexpected change made by a service user is reported, find which user triggered it in the logs and check by role and permission: a user without access to the item (for example only the Contributor role), a profile or folder administrator, and an administrator. A check that passes as an administrator says nothing about a user without access.

probes.abstraction_note: Errors and unexpected writes that only some users trigger are usually permission paths: a read is refused for a user without access, and the backend then falls back to a default path (for example re-creating a shared item) that a service user writes. Testing as an administrator never reproduces it, so it looks intermittent. Counterexample checked: a failure every user gets the same way needs no role split.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: when the failure depends on a setting of the configuration the reporter used (one preset, profile or option), list every other configuration the same item has in the ticket and its attachments (for example another preset of the same map that uses a baseline) and add the reported scenario with them as cases

probes.abstraction_note: A setting on one configuration can be read by shared code for the whole item, so other configurations of the same item (sibling presets, inherited profiles) change the outcome. The reporter's screenshots and videos usually show them. Counterexample checked: an item with only the one configuration needs no extra case.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: when a job or output silently does not do its work, every fix criterion names what QE sees when it works: the changed content in the output itself and the final status shown; a queued or success message, or a successful preprocessing step, is not proof

probes.abstraction_note: Generation and publishing jobs report several statuses (queued, preprocessing finished, warning, success). A criterion that only says the job succeeds can be met by the same misleading status the customer saw. Counterexample checked: a ticket about the status display itself already names the status.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: when a quoted or attached log states the starting state of the item (for example found 0 existing published pages), make that state an explicit precondition of the criterion and cover both states (the item already published and not published yet), or ask in a TBD which one is expected

probes.abstraction_note: Logs often show that the reporter's item was in an unusual starting state (never published, empty, first run), which the steps to reproduce do not mention. A fix tested only on the usual state can miss the reported one. Counterexample checked: a log line about an unrelated item is not a precondition.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: when content in several languages goes into one output, check the text the output template adds: language variables (cross-reference text such as on page, labels such as the chapter number and author label), values from the preset's Variable set, and header and footer text that shows topic metadata; ask in a TBD whether each language section uses its own language or the output language

probes.abstraction_note: A ticket about one mechanism in a multi-language output (for example where a link goes) also puts the template's translated text in play: the template picks one language for its variables, so labels and headers can show the wrong language in the other sections, and any lookup by topic can pick the wrong language copy. Counterexample checked: a single-language output in a translated language is not this case; its labels follow that one language.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: when the action creates new files (from a template, duplicate, copy, new topic or map), check the file naming setting Use UUID based system filenames toggled on and off, and source or target files with GUID file names; links to the new files must use the new file name and topic ID

probes.abstraction_note: Creating files names them by a setting the ticket never mentions (Use UUID based system filenames), and a new topic's topic ID is its file name, so every link to a new file depends on that setting. Counterexample checked: an action that only edits an existing file does not create a name.

implied_dimension.candidate_template: a value users see or change appears on several screens: check every one - the Editor right panel (File properties), the Asset Properties page (Basic tab), Reports > Metadata in the Map console and the Map dashboard - and check as a user who is not an administrator and as an administrator

probes.abstraction_note: A Document State or metadata list is built by the server and shown on several screens, each with its own caller; a fix on one screen leaves the others wrong, and administrators get a different list from other users. Counterexample checked: a value shown on only one screen (for example an output preset field) has no other screen to check.
